body.heading: Choose forgiving food
paragraphs: Some recipes welcome a crowd and some punish it. Pizzas with toppings each person adds, tacos, pasta with a simple sauce, pancakes, and big salads all tolerate extra hands and uneven chopping. Anything that needs precise timing or a clean presentation can wait for a quieter night.
Read the recipe together before starting, out loud, including the boring parts. Most kitchen chaos is really a surprise that nobody read ahead for.

body.heading: Jobs before ingredients
paragraphs: Divide the work before anything comes out of the fridge: one person washes, one measures, one stirs, one is in charge of the timer and the music. Children can do real jobs — tearing herbs, washing vegetables, setting the table, reading the next step aloud.
A bowl on the counter for peelings and scraps, and a sink of warm soapy water ready for used tools, keep the mess small while you cook instead of large afterwards.

body.heading: Finish together too
paragraphs: Build the tidy-up into the meal, not after it. While the food rests or bakes, everyone clears one surface. It takes five minutes together and saves one person a lonely half hour later.
And let the cook be thanked by name. Cooking for a household is daily, skilled work, and a specific thank-you at the table costs nothing and is rarely wasted.

description: Simple shared cooking works when the recipe is forgiving, the jobs are divided early, and tidying happens as you go.
